analysis: Examined all changes. Each of the three workflows (.github/workflows/provider-release-cache.yml head line 25, release-dev-branch.yml line 77, release-swift.yml line 72) only adds 'scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py' to a path trigger filter. No permissions, secrets, runner routing, `if:` conditions, env or step logic changed. The pull_request trigger in provider-release-cache.yml runs with `contents: read` and `persist-credentials: false`, which is unchanged. The push-path additions in release-dev-branch.yml and release-swift.yml mean edits to the script now trigger the signed dev/staging release lanes; those lanes were already triggered by comparable scripts. The script's content is not supplied, so I could not check that the release-build refusal of weak Date comparison imports (the changelog's claim) is implemented or enforced. That is a build-integrity control outside this evidence. The changelog and docs/architecture/security/provider-trust.md additions document an availability issue: SDK 27.2 weak imports of Date >=/<= crash the provider on pre-release macOS builds. The docs state that App Attest stays pending and no authorization is relaxed, which matches TB-011/T-057 (a crash loop causes DoS, not trust elevation). No change to authorization, attestation, encryption, or data exposure. The docs reference scripts/check-date-comparisons.py and a build guide anchor that are not in the supplied evidence. Remaining question: the actual implementation of check-provider-weak-imports.py and its wiring into the release build, which was not provided in this batch.
